    • Monuments

    Lal Bagh

    Lal Bagh is a famous botanical garden which was designed by Hyder Ali. His son Tipu Sultan further augmented this beautiful space in 1760 and later developed by the British as well. Later, during the 19th century, the British added several beautiful features, giving it a modern look. It got its name because of a variety of red flowers that bloom in this garden. Lal Bagh is famous for its flower shows which are held on important occasions, during the Republic Day and the Independence Day. You can also find trees imported from across the world like Persia, France, Afghanistan and China. Some of them being more than a century old.

    Distance from the Hotel: 5.3 kilometres

    Travel Time: 30 minutes

    View Map

    Cubbon Park

    Cubbon Park was built in 1870 by the then Acting Commissioner of Mysore, Sir John Meade. The vast landscape was conceived by the then Chief Engineer of the State, Major General Richard Sankey.
    The park was initially named Meade’s Park, in honour of John Meade and later renamed as Cubbon Park after the longest serving commissioner of the time, Sir Mark Cubbon.
    The park has around 68 varieties and 96 species of flora with about 6000 plants. Many official and public buildings are located within and along its periphery. Indira Priyadarshini Children’s Library, City Central Library, Government Museum, Art Gallery, Aquarium, Yuvanika – the state youth centre, Bal Bhavan (Children’s centre) are located in the park. On weekends, there are several cultural activities which are hosted in the park from theatre to mini marathons.

    Distance from the Hotel: 5.3 kilometres

    Travel Time: 23 minutes

    View Map

    Bugle Rock

    Bugle Rock is estimated to be approximately 3,000 million years old and has an abrupt rise above the ground of the peninsular gneiss as the main rock formation. This rocky outcrop in Bangalore was once used as a lookout point when a monarchy still ruled the city. Whenever there was an assault by the enemy, a bugle call was sounded from this location to warn the town's citizens.

    Distance from the Hotel: 8.1 kilometres

    Travel Time: 35 minutes

    View Map

    National Gallery of Modern Art (NGMA)

    The National Gallery of Modern Art is an art gallery in Bangalore. It was inaugurated in the year 2009. It showcases modern Indian art and houses paintings by Raja Ravi Varma, Jamini Roy, Amrita Sher-Gil, Rabindranath Tagore and a large number of modern and contemporary artists.

    Distance from the Hotel: 4.8 kilometres

    Travel Time: 25 minutes

    View Map

    Tipu Sultan’s Fort and Summer Palace

    This beautiful palace served as a summer retreat for the famous ruler, Tipu Sultan. The construction of this palace was commenced by his father, Nawab Hyder Ali Khan in 1781 and completed by Tipu Sultan in 1791.

    The palace was constructed to house the durbar or court, which would administer the happenings in the territory, while also serving as a summer retreat. This palace is a celebrated destination for Islamic architecture. Tipu Sultan called it an ‘Abode of Happiness’ and ‘Envy of Heaven’.

    Distance from the Hotel: 6.6 kilometres

    Travel Time: 30 minutes

    View Map

    Vidhana Soudha / National Library and Attara Kacheri

    One of the four watchtowers built during the reign of Kempegowda, the founder of Bangalore (during the 15th and 16th centuries), can be found in Bugle Rock garden. As a result, this location is significant in terms of its historical significance.

    Distance from the Hotel: 5 kilometres

    Travel Time: 25 minutes

    View Map

    Dining

    Restaurants
    • Restaurants
    • Bar
    • Lounge
    View all

    BellevueA chic ambience and an Italian soul. Specially curated tasting menus with paired wines guarantees an unforgettable dining experience.

    Cuisine: Italian, Indian, and Pan-Asian.

    Explore

    EsphahanFeast on recipes inherited from the Mughal emperors' kitchens, complemented by soft Indian flatbreads cooked in our tandoor and live traditional music.

    Cuisine: Indian.

    Explore

    The BarUninterrupted Taj Mahal views are best enjoyed from a silk sofa seat or a bar-side stool, with signature cocktails, Oberoi iced teas, and speciality coffees.

    Explore

    The LoungeFrom sunrise until nightfall, watch the play of light on the Taj Mahal through the large windows, from the open-air terrace, or under our crystal chandelier.

    Explore

    Events

    View All

    Roshnara and Jahanara Ballrooms at The Oberoi Amarvilas, Agra. With high ceilings and crystal chandeliers, this is a venue for grand events with up to 190 guests. Can be divided into two halls. Includes an attached pre-function area for food and beverages.

    Explore

    The Bamboo Grove at The Oberoi, Bengaluru. An open-air venue with garden views. Ideal for sunny brunch gatherings, impactful corporate cocktails and exclusive dinner parties for up to 50 guests.

    Explore

    The Grand Ballroom at The Oberoi, Gurgaon. Can host up to 600 people in its entirety or be divided into three smaller venues. With separate guest and service entrances, a pre-function area for food and beverages and views of a water body.

    Explore

    Durbar Hall at The Oberoi Sukhvilas Spa Resort, New Chandigarh. Can be used as a whole for up to 350 guests or divided into two independent venues. With a large, adjoining, al fresco function area.

    Explore

    Grand Canal at The Oberoi, Marrakech. A 120-metre long water body that bisects our 5 star hotel in Morocco. Events held here enjoy breathtaking views of the Atlas Mountains and our gardens. The ideal venue for evening cocktails for up to 400 guests.
